text:
zoe: short one — i'm testing two visual treatments for the heatmap when sampling is low: (1) amber ribbon + small action button, or (2) an inline pill in the header that expands to controls. which is less noisy? :thinking:

mica: pill in header is quieter and keeps focus on the heatmap. ribbon feels like an alert and may clutter dashboards with many panels.

ong: agree with mica, but ribbon is more discoverable for users who never dig into header tools. can we show ribbon only once per session when low sampling is detected?

sam: session-show makes sense. also prefer the pill for default. pill should include a micro-indicator of sample density (e.g., "0.27/s") and an affordance to open quick controls.

zoe: UX follow: quick controls should let users pick presets (Auto, High, Medium, Low) and have an "advanced" link to a slider. keep everything reachable from the pill.

mica: accessibility concerns: the pill needs clear focus state and an aria-describedby pointing to the current sample-rate explanation. screen readers should be told when density changes after a range pan.

a11y-bot: recommend aria-live="polite" on the status region that contains "sampled X per second". also ensure color isn't the only indicator: include an icon (bars) and an explicit word like "Low" for clarity.

ong: contrast nit: the amber badge text fails AA on light backgrounds at 12px. bump text to 13px or add 1px stroke. outline approach seems less intrusive than increasing type size.

sam: dev note: we can compute a contrast flag server-side and send back `showOutline:true` for view rendering. then client just toggles a CSS class. cheap and reliable.

zoe: interaction question: when user increases density, should the UI auto-hide the pill/ribbon? i think yes after a successful manual change. if they pin it, keep it visible.

mica: yes auto-hide unless pinned. also expose a small undo toast: "Density set to High — undo" in case the change causes slow rendering for some users.

a11y-bot: toast should have role="status" and disappear after an accessible timeout (not too fast), and should be focusable so keyboard users can reach the undo.

ong: copy suggestion for pill tooltip: "Observed sample rate for this view. Low rates can exaggerate short spikes. Adjust density for more accurate p95." short, actionable.

sam: another micro: when p95 line is displayed over softened buckets, show small semi-transparent markers at bucket centers on hover and allow keyboard focus to step through marker points with left/right arrows when focused on the chart. helps precise reading.

mica: add a small visual cue for low-confidence p95 points — a dotted connector between confident points. keeps the continuous feel but signals uncertainty.

a11y-bot: announce confidence level in the tooltip: "p95 (low confidence) — 95th percentile calculated from 8 samples". don't require exact numbers if they aren't provided, but make clear when values are approximate.

z oe: final asks: mica/ong — can you mock pill + session ribbon variant with the pinned state and the toast undo? sam — can you hand off the small CSS var for outline toggle so engineers can flip it based on server flag? i'll add this to Friday's design review.

design-bot: reminder: attach accessibility checklist and a one-line telemetry spec: `sample_ui_shown`, `density_changed`, `density_undo_clicked`, `p95_marker_focused`.

sam: i'll post the CSS snippet and a tiny gif by tomorrow.

zoe: thanks everyone — aim to test thresholds on a small cohort before wider rollout. :raised_hands:
